newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Holzmann falls on CEO, cash worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Holzmann falls on CEO, cash worries.

text.p: Shares in German builder Philipp Holzmann AG fell sharply on Friday as reports of liquidity problems and the possible sacking of its chief executive added to existing nervousness about the stock.

Holzmann shares fell 20 marks in early trade to 330 marks, a fall of nearly six percent, despite its denial of a radio report earlier this week that the company had liquidity problems and that its bank credit lines were at risk.

The group also denied a report in the mass circulation daily "Bild" newspaper that its chief executive Lothar Mayer faced dismissal on the findings of an auditor's report into huge charges taken in 1995 on property activities.

But analysts said the two news reports, while denied, had taken their toll on its shares because of the continued uncertainty surrounding Holzmann since it shocked the market last year with news of the 458 million marks ($300 million) of write-downs.

"We've had these new rumours (of liquidity problems) a couple of months ago, but it just adds to the nervousness about Holzmann when they resurface like this," Ingbert Faust, construction analyst at UBS in Frankfurt, said.

Holzmann on Wednesday denied a radio report that its banks had cut its credit lines, repeating a comment made with interim results in August that its financial projections were based on the assumption of sufficient liquidity in 1996 and 1997.

The group on Friday also criticised as "factually incorrect" the Bild report for saying that Mayer's job would be on the line following a presentation next week to its supervisory board of an auditor's report on the write-downs.
The supervisory board said in a statement that it was meeting next Thursday, but that it was simply a regular event that had been scheduled months in advance.
It added that it understood that the report, by auditing group KPMG, contained no new information on the losses.
Diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG had earlier also denied further speculation in the report that its management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen was being mooted to replace Mayer.

Holzmann, which has also suffered badly within the overall weakness in the German contracting sector, has said it expected an operating loss in 1996 after 1995's losses of 443 million marks following the write-downs.
Analysts said that any change of chief executive at Holzmann might have implications for takeover plans that construction rival Hochtief AG has for the company.
Hochtief is currently attempting to overturn a ruling by the German cartel office that the takeover attempt cannot go ahead for competition reasons.
"Mayer was clearly a key figure opposing the takeover plans," one said. ($1=1.5306 Mark)
